files.purpose: This file is the chat column's conversation view for one thread (ThreadTimeline) plus every model type that turns ThreadRuntime.entries into what the view stacks: TimelineGroup (single / work run / heads), DisplayBlock (one block per turn plus synthetic working, merging and headsWorking blocks), TimelineMeta (per-turn summary and reply facts) and TimelineBlockCache (a per-thread memoized build with an append-only fast path). It also owns the whole scroll machinery of the timeline: follow-the-end pinning, choosing the bottom or top anchor for size changes, an identity-anchored lazy window of blocks that loads older history 24 at a time, blank-viewport detection and escalating repair, the AppKit one-point 'nudge' of the enclosing NSScrollView that makes the LazyVStack rebuild for the real viewport, the scroll freeze that disables hit-testing while the reader scrolls, and the FrontMonitor singleton that reports app activation, window uncovering and whole-app visibility. Finally it defines the running turn's working line (WorkingIndicator, WorkingBlockView, TurnRunningBlock), the shared composer/timeline objects TimelineScrollState and TimelineRevealBox, and the revealTimelineEnd environment key.

feature_notes: Block build: entries are split into contiguous runs sharing one turnID (nil runs together). A run with a turnID becomes one .turn block whose entries exclude .turnEnd and .reasoning, id "turn-\(turnID.uuidString)-\(firstEntryID)", summary = meta.summaryByTurn[turnID], showsWorking = isLast && summary == nil && isRunning. A run without a turnID becomes .group blocks from TimelineGroup.build with meta.summary(for:) and meta.hasReply(for:).

If isRunning and the last block does not carry the working line (.turn with showsWorking true), a .working(turnID: entries.last?.turnID, liveWork: []) block is appended; its id is "working-" + uuidString or "working-" with an empty string.

Head pills: while running and pills.earlier is non-empty, a .headsWorking(heads: earlier, trailing: false) block is inserted before the last .turn block with no summary, only if that turn's rows contain no head (.agent tool call). pills.later non-empty appends .headsWorking(heads: later, trailing: isRunning). Ids: "hydra-heads-working-tail" when trailing, else "hydra-heads-working". Finished heads are sorted by finishedAt; earlier = finished before runtime.turnStartedAt while running. Sources (lines 102-131): pills come from `model.helpers(of: runtime.threadID).filter(\.isHydraHead)` (comment: "Every unarchived head, in the panel or not"); mention personas and mention targets come from `model.children(of: runtime.threadID).filter(\.isHydraHead)` (comment: "Every head the chat ever sent out"). `let since = runtime.isRunning ? runtime.turnStartedAt : nil` and `let earlier = since.map { ... } ?? []`, so while running with turnStartedAt nil, earlier is empty and every finished head goes to later.

Merge pill: when hydraMergeID is non-nil (runtime.isHydraMerging ? runtime.hydraMergeNoteID ?? "hydra-merging" : nil) and entries do not end with a merge outcome note, .merging(id:) is appended. isMergeOutcome: message.isFromHydra, hydraHeads nil or empty, and the first non-empty line has prefix "Hydra ". hydraMergePhase maps .merging to .merging and a single user entry that is a merge outcome to .outcome(message), rendered by HydraMergeRow so the pill morphs in place.

TimelineGroup.build: tool entries form work runs split when turnID changes; .agent tool calls go to a heads list appended last as .heads(id: "heads-\(first.id)"); .reasoning entries are skipped; any other kind flushes the run and becomes .single. A work run's id is "work-\(first.id)" and startsCollapsed is true when any assistant entry index lies after the run's end. showReasoning is accepted but unused inside build.

Lazy window (B2): windowStartIndex returns the index of windowStartID if present, else max(0, blocks.count - 3). hidden = startIndex. loadEarlier(in:to:) returns if historyLoadPending; target = count.map { max(0, blocks.count - $0) } ?? max(0, start - 24); returns unless target < start (start only moves back); then sets historyLoadPending, anchorsBottomOnGrowth = true and windowStartID = blocks[target].id. The .task(id: runtime.threadID) sleeps 250 ms, holdEnd(1.0), loadEarlier(to: 24), armBlankWatch, then warmMarkdown. Switching thread sets windowStartID = nil, anchorsBottomOnGrowth = true, historyLoadPending = false, clearVisible(). TimelineWindow (lines 1795-1799): firstPaint = 3, initial = 24, page = 24. Initial-task edge case (B2 behaviour change): with windowStartID nil and blocks.count <= 3, start = max(0, blocks.count - 3) = 0 and target = max(0, blocks.count - 24) = 0, so `guard target < start else { return }` bails: windowStartID stays nil and historyLoadPending stays false. The window then remains the sliding newest-3 suffix (each appended block moves the start forward, the oldest visible block leaves the stack and the "Show \(hidden) earlier messages" pill appears) until the pill's `.onScrollVisibilityChange(threshold: 0.1)` fires `loadEarlier(in: blocks)` (target = max(0, start - 24)), a minimap jump to a hidden block sets windowStartID, or the thread changes. A new thread reaches the timeline branch (and its .task) only once blocks is non-empty or runtime.isRunning (line 136), typically with 1 block. B1's `let target = count ?? visibleCount + TimelineWindow.page; guard target > visibleCount` always set visibleCount = 24 and historyLoadPending = true on the initial task, whatever the thread length. Once windowStartID is set, nothing moves the start forward (loadEarlier only moves it back, jump only to an earlier index; only a thread change resets it to nil, or the anchored block leaving the blocks falls back to the newest 3), so the materialized window grows without bound as blocks are appended; the TimelineWindow doc comment at lines 1789-1790 ("the number of live views stays bounded even for very long threads") is stale in B2 and must not be read as a cap.

Minimap jump: if the target index is before the window start, windowStartID becomes the target id, historyLoadPending true and the scroll is deferred with DispatchQueue.main.async; isPinnedToBottom = (id == last block id); anchorsBottomOnGrowth = pinned || needsExpand; scrollTo(id:, anchor: .top) with .smooth(duration: 0.35) when animated, unanimated otherwise.
Rewind: rewindable = Set(runtime.turns ids) only when supportsRewind && !runtime.isRunning; a row's canRewind is whether its turnID is in that set.

Pinning threshold is 48 pt from the bottom in every place (history landed, scrolled, stale pin, areaGrowthRequest, lastEntryID). readerMoved means |offset delta - anchorMove| > 1 where anchorMove is the content height delta under a bottom anchor. Past-the-end (distanceFromBottom < -1) at rest with a content or container size change snaps to the bottom (deferred, unanimated). Pinned at rest and |distance| > 1 snaps to bottom unless liveResize.isActive. onScrollGeometryChange (lines 483-590): first `scrollChrome.update(travel:)`, `tracking.noteGeometry(...)`, `nudging = tracking.isNudging`, `tracking.noteNudgeSeen()`, wheel detection, readerMoved (then noteReaderMovement), `scrolled = tracking.isUserScrolling || (!nudging && !tracking.isArriving && readerMoved && new.containerHeight == old.containerHeight && !tracking.isCoasting)`, `atRest = !tracking.isUserScrolling && !tracking.isCoasting`, then the drift block (atRest && !scrolled) or resetDrift (scrolled). Then ONE if / else-if chain in this order: (1) `new.distanceFromBottom < -1, atRest, new.contentHeight != old.contentHeight || new.containerHeight != old.containerHeight` -> DispatchQueue.main.async unanimated `position.scrollTo(edge: .bottom)`; (2) `else if historyLoadPending, new.contentHeight > old.contentHeight` -> historyLoadPending = false; pinned = tracking.isPinnedToBottom || new.distanceFromBottom < 48; anchorsBottomOnGrowth = pinned (written only if different); and `if tracking.isPinnedToBottom, new.distanceFromBottom > 1` a DispatchQueue.main.async unanimated scrollTo(edge: .bottom) (a short thread made tall by history is put back on the end); (3) `else if scrolled` -> pinned = new.distanceFromBottom < 48, written to isPinnedToBottom and anchorsBottomOnGrowth when different; (4) `else if (tracking.isPinnedToBottom || old.distanceFromBottom < 48), atRest, abs(new.distanceFromBottom) > 1` -> `guard !liveResize.isActive else { return }`, isPinnedToBottom = true, anchorsBottomOnGrowth = true, then DispatchQueue.main.async unanimated scrollTo(edge: .bottom).

Drift: at rest and not scrolled, drift = shrink + (bottom anchor ? |offset delta - content delta| : |offset delta|); noteDrift triggers armViewportRefresh when accumulated drift exceeds max(48, viewportHeight / 4); a shrink > 1 arms the blank watch.

Sending: onChange(runtime.isRunning) to true resets phase to idle; unattended = seenAutoStartedTurnToken != runtime.autoStartedTurnToken (false when not seen yet); if at end or not unattended, pins and scrolls to bottom (unanimated if already at end, else .easeOut(duration: 0.25)); always armViewportRefresh. To false: deferred bottom snap if pinned, armViewportRefresh, armBlankWatch, warmMarkdown. Right after computing unattended it always stores `seenAutoStartedTurnToken = runtime.autoStartedTurnToken` (line 645), so only a later token change reads as unattended.

lastEntryID = "question-" + last question id, else last visible block id. On change, unless historyLoadPending or user scrolling, a pinned reader, a reader within 48 pt, or a new question brings the view to the bottom unanimated and hides the jump button.
Question count dropping from non-zero to 0 arms a viewport refresh.

repairLayout: requires viewportHeight > 0; if scrolling, sets repairSkippedWhileScrolling. Past the end or pinned-and-away snaps to bottom and, if still showing nothing and blankRepairs < 3, arms a refresh. Otherwise if showing nothing, escalates by blankRepairs: 0 refreshViewport, 1 stackGeneration += 1 plus refresh, 2 pin and snap to bottom plus refresh, 3+ stop. Each action increments blankRepairs and re-arms the 300 ms blank watch.

refreshViewport: skips while nudging or scrolling (sets refreshSkippedWhileScrolling); pinned = isPinnedToBottom && distance <= 1. Prefers beginNudge (1 pt up, or down at the top, only if the constrained move exceeds 0.25), restoring after up to 4 x 17 ms and snapping to bottom if pinned; else if pinned and travel > 1 scrolls to offset - 1 then bottom; else if pinned, endUnseen and not arriving, bumps stackGeneration.
armViewportRefresh: resets drift; coalesces while pending; limits bursts to 8 within a 2 s window; waits up to 12 x 17 ms for a nudge to finish before bumping refreshRequest.

notePhase: isUserScrolling for .interacting or .decelerating; isCoasting for .decelerating or .animating; watch polls every 200 ms and ends the phase after 2.0 s without reader movement for .interacting, 0.4 s otherwise, or 3.0 s total, then withdraws the scrolling report and bumps checkRequest. Details (lines 1084-1111): `if isUserScrolling { drift = 0 }`; the previous phaseWatch is cancelled first; `guard isCoasting || isUserScrolling else { return }`, so .idle cancels the watch and returns without bumping checkRequest; the watch sets isUserScrolling = false and isCoasting = false, withdraws via ScrollActivity.shared.setScrolling(false, timeline: reported) only `if let reported = reportedTimeline, !isReaderScrolling`, then `checkRequest += 1`.

Scroll freeze: noteScrollMovement sets isReaderScrolling and polls every 80 ms, clearing after 0.15 s of no movement; liftScrollFreeze clears immediately on any non-interacting phase. Wheel movement is detected as a centerY change with unchanged content height, not nudging and not coasting.
holdEnd: 1.5 s on scroll view appear, 1.0 s when the initial window loads; isArriving suppresses reading offset changes as reader scrolls.

revealEnd follows only when the jump button is hidden, or pinned, or distanceFromBottom < viewportHeight; followEnd always pins, scrolls to bottom (inside the caller's animation) and calls noteScrollMovement.
settleAfterResize: when a live resize ends, snaps to bottom if pinned, else arms a refresh; always arms the blank watch; while scrolling it only arms a refresh.

FrontMonitor: didBecomeActive bumps with no window (app-wide) and refreshes visibility; didResignActive refreshes visibility; occlusion change refreshes visibility and bumps for that window only if its occlusionState contains .visible. concerns(window) is true when app-wide or the uncovered window is the timeline's window. isVisible = NSApp.isActive && any window isVisible with occlusion .visible. The timeline's onChange(FrontMonitor.shared.revision) calls noteReturnToFront (blankRepairs 0, checkRequest += 1, blank watch, viewport refresh) only when concerns(tracking.probe?.window).

ScrollMetrics: travel = min(max(0, offset.y + inset.top), max(0, contentHeight + insets - containerHeight)); distanceFromBottom = 0 when contentHeight + insets <= containerHeight + 1, else contentHeight + inset.bottom - offset.y - containerHeight.
resolveActive: takes the middle on-screen block (count / 2) and sets activeBlockID to the last user-message block at or above it; nothing changes when no block is on screen.

TimelineBlockCache: key = entry ObjectIdentifiers, count of .turnEnd entries, isRunning, hydraMergeID, pills, showReasoning. Equal key returns cached blocks. extends() (lines 1689-1696) compares only `entries.count > old.entries.count && isRunning == old.isRunning && hydraMergeID == old.hydraMergeID && pills == old.pills && showReasoning == old.showReasoning && entries.starts(with: old.entries)`; turnEnds is NOT compared, so an append that adds a .turnEnd still takes the tail path: rebuild from built.lastRunStart keeping built.blocks[..<stableCount] over meta grown by the new entries; aborts to a full build if a new turnEnd's summary.turnID belongs to a kept block. LRU of 24 thread caches. mentionPersonas memoizes on head indices and roster flag; personas are unique by name, heads first, then HydraRoster.personas when roster (model.hydraIsOn for the thread). buildTail returns nil (full rebuild with `meta = TimelineMeta.build(entries)`) only when an appended .turnEnd's summary.turnID matches a block in built.blocks[..<built.stableCount] (lines 1749-1751), or in DEBUG when the every-20th check differs.
mentionTargets: heads sorted by createdAt ascending, so a reused persona name maps to the newest head.

TimelineMeta: lastAssistantIDByTurn and turnsWithReply from .assistant entries; summaryByTurn from .turnEnd content. summary(for:) only for the turn's last assistant single; hasReply(for:) only for a .turnEnd single.

TurnRunningBlock: groups by TurnGroupCache; a trailing .heads group is removed and rendered after the other rows; .work entries and .single assistant entries go into liveWork (the working card), other groups render as TurnRow; WorkingBlockView shown when showsWorking or liveWork non-empty, with earlierEntries = showsWorking ? nil : entries. The rows sit in a plain `VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: TimelineMetrics.rowSpacing)`, deliberately not lazy (comment: "a lazy stack inside a lazy row resolved its own visibility on every scrolled frame for nothing"); every TurnRow (`.equatable()`), the heads TurnRow and the WorkingBlockView carry `.transition(ThreadTimeline.rowTransition)`.

DisplayBlockView: finished turn (summary non-nil) renders TurnFinishedBlock with user entries split from content, canUndo = context.canRewind, chronological = context.chronological; running turn renders TurnRunningBlock; both .transition(.identity). .merging is unreachable (EmptyView) because hydraMergePhase routes it.

TimelineGroupView: .user UserMessageRow(canRevert: canRewind); .assistant AssistantMessageRow(summary); .reasoning EmptyView; .tool single WorkGroup; .plan PlanCard; .todos TodoListRow; .notice NoticeRow; .turnEnd TurnEndRow(summary, hasReply); .work WorkGroup(startsCollapsed); .heads HydraHeadsList.

WorkingBlockView: startedAt = earlierEntries first date ?? runtime.turnStartedAt ?? now; seed = WorkingWords.seed(threadID.uuidString); thinking only when earlierEntries == nil and settings.showReasoning; finishedAt = earlierEntries last date; turnEntries walks back from the last entry's turnID, skipping nil-turn entries, stopping at another turn. WorkingIndicator.onChange(chronological, initial: true) sets isExpanded and showsAllSteps to chronological. thinking keeps only `entry.kind == .reasoning, case .reasoning(let block) = entry.item.content, !block.text.isEmpty`, so empty reasoning entries are dropped; both turnEntries(of:) and thinking start with `guard let turnID = runtime.entries.last.flatMap(\.turnID) else { return [] }`, so both are empty when the last entry has no turnID.

B1->B2: (1) The lazy window changed from a count to an identity anchor: @State visibleCount = TimelineWindow.firstPaint was replaced by @State windowStartID: String?, with the new windowStartIndex(in:) (falls back to the newest firstPaint = 3 blocks when the id is nil or gone), so once windowStartID is set, appending a block at the end no longer evicts the oldest visible row; while windowStartID is nil (source comment: "Nil until the thread anchors, when the newest `firstPaint` blocks are the window") windowStartIndex is max(0, blocks.count - 3) and still slides forward on every append, and in B2 the initial loadEarlier(in: blocks, to: 24) leaves it nil for threads with blocks.count <= 3 (see the lazy window note), whereas B1's initial loadEarlier always set visibleCount = 24 and historyLoadPending = true; timeline() computes hidden = startIndex and visible = blocks[startIndex...] instead of blocks.suffix(visibleCount). (2) loadEarlier() became loadEarlier(in blocks:, to count:), computing a target start index (max(0, blocks.count - count) or max(0, start - 24)) and moving the start only backwards (guard target < start); jump(to:) sets windowStartID = blocks[index].id instead of visibleCount = blocks.count - index; the thread-change handler sets windowStartID = nil instead of visibleCount = firstPaint; timelineScroll gained a blocks: parameter to pass to loadEarlier. (3) The per-row modifier chain moved out of the LazyVStack's ForEach into a new private func row(_:rewindable:) (comment: the view builder timed the compiler out); the explanatory comments on onScrollVisibilityChange / onDisappear were dropped. (4) The row's RowContext now passes chronological: false instead of model.settings.chronologicalTimeline, so the timeline rows no longer follow the chronologicalTimeline setting from this file. The same B1->B2 range adds the setting to AppSettings.swift (Key `static let chronologicalTimeline = "chronologicalTimeline"`, didSet `defaults.set(chronologicalTimeline, forKey: Key.chronologicalTimeline)`, load `defaults.object(forKey: Key.chronologicalTimeline) as? Bool ?? false`); B1's Swift sources read model.settings.chronologicalTimeline in ThreadTimeline without defining it anywhere, and in B2 a git grep finds no reader of it, only the AppSettings definition and doc comments at ThreadTimeline.swift:1861 and TimelineRows.swift:2492: the key is persisted but inert. (5) The @Environment(\.chatZoom) zoom property was removed from both ThreadTimeline and WorkingIndicator, and the three .font(.chat(..., zoom: zoom)) calls became .font(.chat(.callout)), .font(.chat(.caption2, weight: .semibold)) and .font(.chat(.callout)); a grep of the B2 Swift sources finds no chatZoom anywhere. Line count 2298 -> 2314 (60 insertions, 44 deletions).

timelineScroll evaluation side effects (lines 345-358): `if tracking.setOutline(visible.map { ($0.id, $0.hasUserMessage) })` (setOutline returns true only when the id list differs; it then updates outlineIDs, outlineSet, userBlockIDs and calls resolveActive()) calls `tracking.armBlankWatch()` and `if tracking.isPinnedToBottom, !tracking.isArriving { tracking.armViewportRefresh() }`; every evaluation also reassigns `revealBox.action = revealEnd` and `revealBox.follow = followEnd`.

setVisible / clearVisible (lines 993-1012): on visible, `guard visibleIDs.insert(id).inserted else { return }`, then cancels and nils blankWatch and sets `blankRepairs = 0` (a row coming back ends the repair sequence); on hidden, `guard visibleIDs.remove(id) != nil else { return }`, then `if showsNothing { armBlankWatch() }`; both changed paths then call resolveActive(). clearVisible() empties visibleIDs and sets activeBlockID to nil (written only if not already nil). showsNothing = `!outlineIDs.isEmpty && visibleIDs.isDisjoint(with: outlineSet)`.

Deferred work and request counters: on `.onScrollPhaseChange` with `phase == .idle` (lines 472-481), `if tracking.repairSkippedWhileScrolling { tracking.repairSkippedWhileScrolling = false; tracking.armBlankWatch() }` and `if tracking.refreshSkippedWhileScrolling { tracking.refreshSkippedWhileScrolling = false; tracking.armViewportRefresh() }`. `.onChange(of: tracking.checkRequest)` (lines 605-611) calls `tracking.reportActivity(timeline: runtime.threadID)` then `repairLayout()`; `.onChange(of: tracking.refreshRequest)` (lines 658-660) calls `refreshViewport()`. armBlankWatch (lines 1116-1123) cancels any previous watch, sleeps 300 ms and bumps checkRequest only if `guard let self, !Task.isCancelled, showsNothing else { return }` passes at fire time.

Synthetic .working block (lines 1592, 1915-1916): built only as `.working(turnID: entries.last?.turnID, liveWork: [])` and rendered as `WorkingBlockView(runtime: runtime, liveWork: liveWork, workingDirectory: context.workingDirectory)` with chronological at its default false and earlierEntries nil. So it is always a live running line: finishedAt nil, liveWork empty, label `"\(word)…"` (hasTools false), canExpand = !thinkingSteps.isEmpty, i.e. expandable only when settings.showReasoning is on and the last turn has non-empty reasoning.

DisplayBlock.turnID and hasUserMessage (lines 1501-1517): turnID is `turnID` for .turn and `entry.turnID` for .group(.single(entry)); .group(.work), .group(.heads), .working, .merging and .headsWorking return nil, so they never get canRewind. hasUserMessage is `entries.contains { $0.kind == .user }` for .turn, `entry.kind == .user` for .group(.single), false for all others; it feeds setOutline's userBlockIDs (rail ticks) and the minimap condition `showsMinimap, blocks.count(where: \.hasUserMessage) > 1` (line 180).

Sliding-sidebar layout width (lines 59-66, 454-458): layoutWidth is nil unless `liveResize.isReshaping, paneWidth > 0`; the slide formula min(820 + 40, max(12, paneWidthAtSlideStart + model.sidebar.slideDelta)) applies only when `model.sidebar.isSliding, paneWidthAtSlideStart > 0`, else min(820 + 40, floor(paneWidth / 12) * 12). paneWidthAtSlideStart is captured only by `.onChange(of: model.sidebar.isSliding) { _, sliding in if sliding { paneWidthAtSlideStart = paneWidth } }` and is not reset when the slide ends.
unresolved_questions: Whether upstream intends to wire chronologicalTimeline to a control later is unknown; at B2 the key is defined and persisted in AppSettings.swift (added in the B1->B2 diff) but read nowhere (git grep of the B2 tree finds no reader or settings binding), and ThreadTimeline.row hardcodes chronological: false, so parity means the working card and TurnFinishedBlock always behave as chronological == false.
Font.chat(_:weight:) signature and behavior after chatZoom's removal is defined elsewhere (not in this file); the Windows port must read that definition to size the pill and working line text.

Values of TimelineMetrics (rowSpacing, pillLeading, pillTrailing, pillVertical, pillRadius, iconWidth, iconSpacing), Chrome.contentTopInset, Chrome.panelSlide, Chrome.accent, WindowChrome.titlebarHeight, Animation.softAppear and SoftAppearModifier are defined in other files and are not given here.

Whether the Windows scroll/virtualization stack exhibits the LazyVStack blank-viewport failure that the nudge / stackGeneration repair addresses is not decidable from this file; parity of the observable behavior (never showing an empty pane, snapping to the end) is the requirement.
